To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a meta two-sample testing algorithm that improves over the state of the art in the regime of limited data.

we propose the problem of meta-two-sample testing, which aims to find a kernel-based two-sample test algorithm that can quickly find a powerful test on a new task given abundant auxiliary data on related problems, and we show that our proposed algorithms outperform learning two-sample tests directly from limited data.

(1) meta two-sample testing is a promising direction to improve two-sample tests with limited data, (2) our proposed methods are effective for this task, (3) our methods are particularly useful for distinguishing distributions that are close together, and (4) our methods can be used to improve other kernel-based learning tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning from data that are both scarce and high-dimensional.
meta-learning of kernels for two-sample testing.
the problem of learning a powerful kernel to distinguish distributions from very few samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose two meta two-sample testing schemes that outperform learning kernel based tests from scarce observations and we identify when these schemes will be successful.
our meta two-sample testing algorithms can significantly outperform the baselines, and can be used to learn powerful kernel-based tests from limited data.
the meta-testing scheme can learn the optimal kernel from limited data, while the learning kernel-based testing directly from limited data can not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of limited samples, meta two-sample testing is an effective and practical approach to distinguish complex distributions in high dimensions.
, by leveraging the power of meta-learning, we are able to learn powerful two-sample tests from very few samples.
we introduce M2ST, propose two specific schemes, and provide both theoretical and empirical evidence to support the usefulness of M2ST.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when data are scarce, it is often better to learn a kernel-based test from a related task, even when the related task itself is not of primary interest.
, in many settings, meta-learning is a promising approach for learning powerful kernels for two-sample testing.
, when data is scarce, it is possible to leverage auxiliary data to learn a powerful test.
